Relatives described unresponsiveness with staring spells, convulsions starting in the right face and arm, and generalized convulsions; postictal findings included somnolence, disorientation and Todd’s paresis of the right upper and lower limbs.

History revealed two epileptic episodes during sleep in the previous 1.5 years, a generalized tonic–clonic seizure and status epilepticus, after which levetiracetam and phenytoin were initiated but later discontinued. Relatives reported recent memory impairment and disorientation.

Examination showed brisk deep tendon reflexes and positive grasp reflexes, ACE-R score was 56, brain CT showed global atrophy and EEG showed slow-sharp waves at 6 Hz over the left anterior temporal region. MCI in the context of epilepsy was diagnosed and levetiracetam dosage was increased; follow-up EEGs at 6 and 18 months showed no epileptiform abnormalities.
